findings.text: _processes_holding re-implements the repository's process-holder scan owned by reckon/crew/gc.py:1713 (the same helper re-exported through reckon/crew/routing.py and used by reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py:2198) instead of extending or sharing that owner; the two now differ in semantics (gc matches a path or anything beneath it and returns a list of dicts, this one matches only the file and returns pids or None), so the repository has two drifting answers to one question.

_index_lock_age_seconds duplicates reckon/crew/promotion_scope.py:2029, which already computes the same checkout's index.lock age under the identical name and is the older owner; the copies differ in taking a lock path versus a checkout and in clamping negatives, so the age of one lock is now defined twice.

every other caller of the shared wait helper (promotion_scope.py:1900, :2496, :2629 and ledger.py:3182, :3216) now clears a provably stale lock but passes no on_stale_removed, so those paths deletes a lock with nothing in the landing record naming it; the plan's 'one line naming the lock's age and that it was removed goes to the landing's own record' holds only for land_merge, as the landed fragment's scope note admits.

the done_when's 'at the base revision the first case refuses' has no recorded arm: the base arm removes the new test rather than running it against the base reckon/crew/merge.py, so the reported defect's reproduction is inferred from the passing head case and no log quotes it; running the case against the base module and capturing its red EXIT would close it.

the tests field is a prose description of the gate rather than the literal command a shell ran, which the delivery contract says promotion cannot re-run and refuses; the literal command survives only in each log's '# command:' header, so the field should be replaced with the head arm's exact command line before promotion.
